evals.prompt: У нас двойные бронирования слотов. PostgreSQL (read committed), два инстанса сервиса. Код: SELECT считает существующие брони слота, если count == 0 — INSERT. Под нагрузкой в один слот периодически попадают две брони. Диагностируй: покажи ломающий schedule, выбери минимальный механизм, определи путь конфликта для проигравшего (что вернуть клиенту) и дай executable тест, который форсит гонку и падает без фикса. Прод и код не меняй.
evals.expected_output: A diagnosis naming the check-then-act schedule under read committed, the weakest fix as a unique or exclusion constraint with a handled conflict surfaced to the caller, and a barrier-forced two-writer test that fails without the mechanism.
expectations: Constructs the explicit two-actor schedule — both SELECTs see zero, both INSERT — and names it check-then-act legal under read committed.
Chooses the weakest sufficient rung: a unique or exclusion constraint arbitrating the insert race, with reasons for rejecting heavier options like FOR UPDATE or serializable.
Designs the loser path: the constraint violation is handled and surfaced as a conflict response with enough context to re-decide, not blindly retried with stale intent.
Lists both replicas and request retries as writers and explains why an in-process mutex cannot close the schedule.
Provides a deterministic test forcing the interleaving with a barrier or injected pause at the check, asserting one booking, and failing when the constraint is removed.
Adds a real-store stress assertion of the invariant and notes that in-memory fakes do not arbitrate like the real engine.
Keeps production and code unchanged with the fix labeled proposed.

evals.prompt: Спроектируй списание с баланса кошелька: баланс не может уйти в минус, по горячим кошелькам сотни конкурентных списаний в секунду, плюс клиенты ретраят запросы. Сравни атомарный условный UPDATE, optimistic versioning и SELECT FOR UPDATE для этого кейса, выбери минимальный, определи путь конфликта и ретраев, идемпотентность повторов, и докажи инвариант stress-тестом с N писателями.
evals.expected_output: A comparison landing on the atomic conditional UPDATE as the weakest closing rung for non-negativity under hot-key contention, idempotent retry composition via stable operation identity, bounded conflict dispositions, and an N-writer real-store stress proof.
expectations: Compares the three mechanisms against the hot-key contention profile and picks the atomic conditional UPDATE with checked row count as the weakest rung closing non-negativity.
Explains why optimistic versioning thrashes on hot keys and names the conditions under which FOR UPDATE would be justified instead.
Separates the balance invariant from effect identity: client retries carry a stable operation identity so a retried debit cannot double-spend.
Distinguishes the insufficient-funds outcome from a concurrency conflict and bounds any retries with attempts, time, and jitter.
Addresses the aggregate invariant if a ledger is introduced — balance matches entries — and names the mechanism guarding it.
Provides a stress proof with N concurrent writers plus injected retries at the real store, asserting no negative balance and one effect per operation identity.
States the assumed isolation level and the residual windows of the chosen design.

evals.prompt: Ревью: коллега обернул генерацию месячного инвойса в Redis-lock (SET NX EX 30) и говорит, что теперь два воркера точно не сгенерируют инвойс дважды. Воркеры иногда работают по 2-3 минуты из-за медленного PDF. Проверь рассуждение, покажи, где оно ломается, и предложи минимальную корректную схему. Прод не меняй.
evals.expected_output: A review refuting lock-as-mutual-exclusion — the 30-second TTL expires during the 2-3 minute run and yields two holders — and requiring correctness from the effect side: a stable per-period invoice effect key with a unique claim, or fencing checked at write time; job mechanics routed to durable-background-jobs.
expectations: Constructs the stale-holder schedule: the TTL expires mid-run, a second worker acquires, the first resumes and writes.
States that a distributed lock is expiring advice rather than mutual exclusion and that raising the TTL or adding renewal only narrows the window.
Moves correctness to the effect: a stable invoice-period effect key with a unique claim or ledger, or a fencing generation checked at write time.
Keeps the loser path defined: the second claimant converges on the existing invoice instead of erroring or duplicating.
Routes the recurring-work mechanics — claims, retries, occurrence identity — to durable-background-jobs while retaining the interleaving analysis.
Provides a falsifier: pause the first holder past the TTL, let the second run, resume the first, assert a single invoice and a rejected stale write.
Keeps the review read-only with the fix labeled proposed.

evals.prompt: У нас 4 инстанса сервиса, ежедневный отчёт должен строиться ровно один раз в сутки. Лидер выбирается строкой в PostgreSQL с heartbeat; после failover уже дважды получали два отчёта за день. Спроектируй фикс: fencing, идентичность occurrence, поведение при перекрытии лидеров, и тесты, которые форсят паузу и failover.
evals.expected_output: A design that accepts leader overlap as unavoidable and makes effects safe: a monotonic leadership generation fencing conditional writes plus a per-day occurrence identity with a unique claim, sized heartbeat and expiry windows, and forced-pause and failover tests proving one report.
expectations: States that at-most-one-active leadership is unattainable across pauses and failover and reframes the goal as fenced or idempotent effects under overlap.
Introduces a monotonic leadership generation with conditional writes so a resumed stale leader is rejected at the effect.
Gives each daily occurrence a stable identity with a unique claim so two overlapping leaders converge on one report.
Sizes heartbeat and expiry from measured runtime and pause tails and states the resulting overlap window explicitly.
Covers the crash-while-leading and pause-resume windows with guards and operator-visible signals.
Provides tests that force the overlap: pause the old leader past expiry, promote a new one, resume the old, assert one report and a rejected stale write.
Routes recurring-schedule mechanics to durable-background-jobs where relevant instead of redesigning the queue.

evals.prompt: Инвариант: в смене всегда остаётся минимум один дежурный. Код перед снятием с дежурства проверяет COUNT дежурных > 1 и делает UPDATE своей строки. Под read committed два человека сняли себя одновременно, и смена осталась пустой. Объясни аномалию, почему это не лечится уникальным constraint, сравни варианты (serializable + retry, FOR UPDATE на якорной строке, материализованный инвариант) и выбери минимальный. Дай deterministic тест.
evals.expected_output: An explanation of write skew — overlapping predicate reads followed by disjoint writes, legal under read committed and snapshot levels — a comparison of serializable-with-retry, anchor-row locking, and a materialized invariant row, a justified weakest choice, and a deterministic two-actor proof.
expectations: Names the anomaly write skew: both transactions read an overlapping predicate and write disjoint rows, so no single-row mechanism triggers.
Explains why a unique constraint cannot express a cross-row minimum invariant.
Compares serializable isolation with serialization-failure retries, pessimistic locking of an anchor row, and a materialized counter or invariant row with a conditional update.
Picks the weakest mechanism for the stated load with reasons for rejecting the others, and defines the conflict and retry path for losers.
States the isolation level each option assumes and the residual anomalies it admits.
Provides a deterministic proof forcing the overlapping-read schedule that fails without the mechanism and passes with it.
Routes durable constraint modeling beyond the race to postgres-schema-design and keeps scope on the interleaving.
